fields.meta_description: Build a family law intake form with sections for divorce, custody, and child support, plus a safe way to contact each client. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Family Law Intake Form That Asks What Each Case Needs
fields.hero_description: Build a family law intake form that opens divorce, custody, or support questions by case, saved to a database you own.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Family Law Intake Form
fields.features_heading: What the Attorney Reads Before the Consult
fields.features_subheading: Each section opens from one answer, the case type. A custody client never scrolls past questions about the house.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the case type

Pick divorce and the form asks for the marriage date, the separation date, and any house the couple owns. Pick custody and it asks for each child's age and the current schedule.
fields.feature_2:
A safe way to reach the client

The client picks how the firm may reach them: email only, calls, or texts. That choice sits at the top of the intake, and no one leaves a voicemail on a phone someone else checks.
fields.feature_3:
The other party's name, checked first

Before an attorney reads a word, the app compares the other party's name with the firm's client list. Any match waits for the person who runs conflict checks at the firm.
fields.feature_4:
Pay stubs read into fields

Clients upload pay stubs, and the app reads the employer and gross pay into fields. A value it cannot read with confidence goes to a paralegal to confirm before the consult.
fields.feature_5:
Each case type sent to its owner

A divorce that lists a house can email a partner while custody intakes post to the family team's Slack channel. Every intake also lands as a row in a database the firm owns.
fields.feature_6:
The code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the intake wherever the firm keeps client systems. Keep building on it there, or keep prompting Emergent.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Cases, Four Sets of Questions
fields.tab_content_1:
Thaddeus gets every divorce that lists a house

Linnea Sorensby picks divorce on the Wendmere Family Law intake. She enters a June 2014 marriage and a March 2026 separation, then lists a house she and her spouse own together. Any divorce that lists a house goes to partner Thaddeus Wren by email. Divorces without one wait in the associate queue.
fields.tab_content_2:
One row for each child, ages 6 and 9

Barnaby Keel has 2 children, and the Hartwick Kane Law intake gives each one a row with an age: 6 and 9. He describes the current schedule, every other weekend with him, and uploads the 2023 parenting order. Paralegal Esperanza Tull opens one record with both children and the order attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two pay stubs read into fields, one line left for Corwin

Two pay stubs arrive with Marisa Delacroix's child support intake at Corrigan Pell Law. The app reads her employer, Calder Freight, and her gross pay of $2,240 for each 2-week period into fields. The overtime line came through unreadable. Paralegal Corwin Ashe confirms that value before her consult.
fields.tab_content_4:
On her record, email only and never a call

Odalys Fairbank checks one box on the Ambrey Lane Family Law intake: contact by email only, no calls. She also answers yes to the question about a protective order. Any yes to that question emails managing attorney Hollis Grant on submit, with Email only, no calls printed above every other answer.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Family Law Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Plan a family law intake form case type by case type in seven steps, then build it with Emergent and send a test intake.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the cases the firm takes
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the questions for each case
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask how the firm may reach the client
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the matters the firm accepts, such as divorce, custody, child support, and protective orders. Each one becomes a case type the client picks on the first screen. A matter the firm does not take can show a referral page instead.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Under each case type, list what an attorney asks in a first consult and nothing more. A divorce section might carry dates and property, while a custody section covers the children and how their time is split now. Cut any question no attorney reads.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a contact preference near the top of the form: email only, calls, or texts, and whether a voicemail is safe. Show that answer first on the record. Staff then follow it before they read anything else in the intake.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the papers an attorney wants before the consult, such as a current court order or the 2 most recent pay stubs. Give each upload a plain label, like Current court order, and clients put each document in the right place.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick an owner for each case type and how they hear about it: email for one partner, a Slack channel for the family team. Add a rule for anything urgent, such as a yes to the protective order question. Name a backup for days off.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the case types, questions, uploads, and routing into one prompt. Emergent builds the family law intake form, the database behind it, and a screen where staff review each intake. Change any question later by describing the change.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in a test intake as a made-up custody client with 2 children and a fake court order. Check that the right person gets the email, that the contact preference shows first, and that each child lands in a row of its own.

faq_plan.q: What is a family law intake form?
faq_plan.a: A family law intake form is the questionnaire a prospective client fills in before a first consultation with a family law attorney. It records the client's details, the type of case, the other party's name, and facts such as children, dates, and property. The attorney reads it before the consult starts.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a family law intake form?
faq_plan.a: List the case types the firm takes and the questions each one needs, then decide who receives each intake. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and change any question later by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a divorce intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with both spouses' full names and the dates of marriage and separation. Add any children, the home and other property the couple holds, debts in either name, and each spouse's employer. Ask whether a case is already filed and in which county, and leave the reasons for the divorce to the consult.

faq_plan.q: How much should a family law intake form ask about money and debts?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what the first consult needs: each spouse's employer and gross pay, the home and other large assets, and the debts in each name with a rough balance. Leave full account statements for later in the case. If the firm also handles bankruptcy, give those clients a separate bankruptcy intake form rather than adding a full debt list here.

faq_plan.q: How should a family law intake form handle a client's safe contact details?
faq_plan.a: Ask how and when the firm may contact the client before anything else, and whether it is safe to leave a voicemail or send mail home. Keep that answer at the top of the record. Send a plain confirmation email with no case details in the subject line.

faq_plan.q: Should a family law intake form ask for the other party's information?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the other party's full name and any former names, and run the firm's conflict check on them before an attorney reads the intake. Keep the other party's address and phone optional, and tell the client to leave a field blank rather than guess.

faq_plan.q: How long should a family law intake form take to fill in?
faq_plan.a: Aim for about 10 minutes on the questions every client answers, and let the case type open the rest. If the firm already has a legal intake form, reuse its contact and conflict questions as the opening screens. Then add the family sections after them, and no client answers the same question twice.

faq_plan.q: Can clients upload court orders and pay stubs to a family law intake form?
faq_plan.a: They can on a form built with Emergent. Let clients photograph a paper order with the phone camera instead of scanning it, and mark the pay stub upload optional for custody-only cases. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can a family law intake form work well on a phone?
faq_plan.a: One built with Emergent can, as a conversational flow with one question per screen. Put the uploads on the final screens, after every question is answered. Then send the link to your own phone and finish a full intake before the firm shares it.

faq_plan.q: Can a family law intake form also cover other practice areas?
faq_plan.a: One form built with Emergent can, if the first question asks the type of matter and each answer opens its own sections. A firm that also takes accident cases might keep a separate personal injury intake form and link to it from that first screen.
